passage: The tap in our kitchen dripped all night, and I decided to fix it with a video. First I turned off the water at the small valve, opened the tap to empty it, and laid a cloth over the drain. I unscrewed the cap, swapped the old rubber washer for a new one, and turned the water back on. No drip! I was so proud I made tea for my flatmate Varun and showed him. Then, feeling brave, I tried the leaking joint of the pipe under the sink. The leak got worse. I turned off the valve, put a bucket under it and called a plumber. I had learned which jobs are mine. Asif

qa.q: What did Asif swap for a new one to stop the drip?
qa.a: Asif swapped the old rubber washer for a new one.

qa.q: What was Asif feeling when the drip stopped, and how did that change on the pipe joint?
qa.a: Asif felt proud when the drip stopped, then dismayed when the leak got worse at the pipe joint.

qa.q: What was the wise choice Asif made after the leak got worse?
qa.a: Asif turned off the valve, put a bucket under the leak and called a plumber, since the joint was beyond a video-guided job.

qa.q: How might Varun have seen Asif's tap fix?
qa.a: Varun probably saw a flatmate who was clearly pleased, since Asif made tea and showed the working tap.

grounding: Shows a young adult fixing a small leak with a video and knowing which jobs need a professional.

passage: Repair shop note. Sarita came in on Saturday with a phone in two pieces. She had watched a video and tried to replace the cracked screen herself. She had pried the glass up with a kitchen knife, and it had cracked further; the thin cable was torn. She stood there red-eyed, quiet, half proud of having tried. I told her plainly that the screen swap is a job for a shop because the battery sits right under it and can be damaged. I asked her to bring a broken old phone next time to practise on. She nodded and asked if she could watch me. I said yes. Sharmila, shop owner

qa.q: What did Sarita use to pry the glass up?
qa.a: Sarita used a kitchen knife to pry the glass up.

qa.q: What was Sarita probably feeling as she stood there red-eyed and quiet?
qa.a: Sarita was probably disappointed and embarrassed, yet still a little proud of having tried.

qa.q: What could Sarita do to keep learning about repairs safely?
qa.a: Sarita could practise on a broken old phone and watch a shop repair, leaving jobs near the battery to the shop.

qa.q: How does Sharmila see Sarita's attempt?
qa.a: Sharmila sees a student who was curious and tried hard, and says plainly which job is for a shop while welcoming her to watch.

grounding: Shows a young adult trying a video-guided phone screen repair, dismayed when it fails, and learning which jobs need a professional.
